text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a spike in 95p latency for hosted inference in eu-west from ~120ms to ~1.4s between 02:10-02:20 UTC. Correlated with a batch of idle GPU node drains; a bunch of pods went Pending and triggered cold starts.
jia: thanks, can you paste the alert and the node drain events?
maria: alert: "pending-pods > 5 for >30s in eu-west-ws". From cluster events: several nodepool autoscaler cycles removed 6 gpu nodes within 5m. The warm pool was at 0 because of last-night cron shrink.
jia: hmm — was that cron for cost-savings? we set it to scale-to-zero for low-usage windows but maybe too aggressive.
sam: fwiw the cluster-autoscaler has a pretty short scan period and our drain cooldown default is 0s, so it will remove nodes fast if utilization dips. We also have no regional weighting; eu-west saw the most evictions.
lia: we intentionally set the warm pool to 0 overnight to save $$, but I agree it's biting us. The hosted API SLO is 200ms tail, so these cold starts are unacceptable.
nate: suggestion: add a policy that prevents gpu nodepool from going below N nodes during business hours and applies a longer cooldown for scale-down at night if pending_pods > 0. Also consider node draining jitter so we don't remove several at once.
maria: can we try a small change: set warm pool min_size=1 for eu regions, and set scale-down-unneeded-time to 15m (was 2m) and add a 10m cooldown window after a scale-up before scale-down is allowed?
sam: that sounds reasonable. Example CA config to tweak:
```yaml
clusterAutoscaler:
  scaleDown:
    enabled: true
    delayAfterAdd: 10m  # don't scale down immediately after scale-up
    delayAfterDelete: 10m
    delayAfterFailure: 10m
    unneededTime: 15m
  maxNodeProvisionTime: 20m
```
jia: we should make it region-aware. Maybe override unneededTime and warm-pool min for eu-west and ap-south separately. eu-west gets min_warm=1, unneeded=15m; us-west can stay at min_warm=0, unneeded=5m.
lia: also add a quick-net test: ensure network pulls for model artifacts aren't blocked during scale-up. One root cause before was slow image pull from our registry in eu-west. ops-bot: deploy bot comment: scheduled job 'shrink-warmpools' ran at 01:55 UTC (job id 8621) and removed warm pools in eu-west and ap-south.
nate: can we gate the shrink job with a cheap predictive check: if recent pending_pods rate > 0.5/min then skip shrink. That would avoid cutting warm pools under churn.
sam: alternative: maintain one small kept-warm node with a taint and a tiny watchdog pod that keeps GPU warm (no billing difference if idle vs fully torn down?), need to validate cost math.
maria: cost note — 1 small warm GPU node in eu-west is ~0.6x the overnight billing vs having 0 cold-starts causing customer-facing errors. We should run a quick cost vs latency simulation.
jia: ops plan: 1) revert shrink cron for eu-west, set warm pool min=1; 2) bump CA unneededTime to 15m for eu regions; 3) add drain jitter to max 60s; 4) run loadtest tonight at 02:00 UTC to validate.
lia: test checklist: ensure image pull <30s for model init, KV cache priming <10s for common prefixes, pending_pods recovery <90s.
sam: I'll open a quick PR with the CA YAML and the cron guard, and add a feature-flagged rollout so we can flip back if cost isn't tolerable.
maria: tagging for visibility @ops @infra — we should also update runbook for scale-to-zero incidents.
ops-bot: incident note created: INC-2026-0813-3 (auto) — assigned to eng-infra on-call.
nate: one more: consider region-aware prewarm windows tied to historical traffic: eu-west has a late-night batch at 02:00 UTC sometimes; we can schedule temporary warmup 01:45-02:30.
jia: good idea, I'll run a query against prometheus to produce a heatmap and propose time windows.
maria: thanks team — if everyone OK, proceed with the warm-pool and CA changes, run the loadtest, and we reconvene in #eng-infra in the morning for postmortem. :thumbsup:
